newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BOE moves step towards Maastricht rules-de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: BOE moves step towards Maastricht rules-de Silguy.

text.p: Finance Minister Gordon Brown's decision to give the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates is a significant step towards meeting the Maastricht Treaty requirements on central bank independence, European monetary affairs commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said on Monday.
A spokesman for de Silguy told reporters that Brown had briefed de Silguy and Commission President Jacques Santer on the Bank's new powers.
"It goes in the right direction as far as central bank independence as required by the Treaty is concerned," the spokesman quoted de Silguy as saying.

Brown, in Brussels for his first meeting with EU finance ministers since Labour's landslide election victory, was about to hold discussions with commissioner Mario Monti on Labour's plans to cut VAT on heating fuel to five percent from eight.
Earlier, a Treasury official, said the plan was legally watertight and would be part of Brown's first budget, expected in June or July.
